title: IAM Access Policy Grants Wildcard Administrator Role Across All Services
description: An IAM policy binds the Administrator role across all cloud services (serviceType: *) with account-wide scope, granting complete unrestricted administrative compromise authority.
rationale: Overprivileged administrator policies violate the Principle of Least Privilege. If credentials assigned this policy are compromised, the adversary gains total control over billing, data storage, networking, and security logging.

remediation.summary: Scope the IAM policy to explicit target services and resource groups rather than account-wide wildcards (*).
remediation.ibmcloud_cli:
ibmcloud iam user-policy-delete <IAM_ID> <POLICY_ID> --force
ibmcloud iam user-policy-create <IAM_ID> --roles Viewer,Operator --service-name cloud-object-storage
remediation.console_steps:
1. In IBM Cloud Console, open Manage > Access (IAM) > Users (or Access Groups).
2. Select the assigned identity > Access policies.
3. Delete the account-wide wildcard policy.
4. Re-assign permissions strictly constrained to required services and resource groups.

title: Account-Level Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Not Enforced
description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is set to 'NONE' at the IBM Cloud account level, allowing users to authenticate using only static passwords without a secondary verification factor.
rationale: Single-factor password authentication exposes enterprise cloud infrastructure to credential stuffing, phishing, and password reuse breaches.

remediation.summary: Enforce MFA for all users in the account using IBM Cloud Identity settings (TOTP or Security Key).
remediation.console_steps:
1. Go to Manage > Access (IAM) in IBM Cloud Console.
2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
3. Under 'Authentication', set Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to 'For all users (TOTP4ALL)'.

title: Service ID Possesses Excessive Manager Privileges Across Resource Groups
description: A programmatic Service ID (often used by automated CI/CD pipelines) is granted Manager/Operator roles with wildcard resource group bindings.
rationale: Automated pipeline keys stored in git repositories or build environments can leak. An unconstrained Service ID allows attackers to pivot across distinct security zones.

remediation.summary: Bind Service IDs only to the specific resource group of their workload and restrict roles to the minimum required.
remediation.console_steps:
1. Navigate to Manage > Access (IAM) > Service IDs.
2. Select the Service ID > Access Policies.
3. Edit the policy to specify the exact Resource Group instead of 'All Resource Groups'.

title: Dormant or Unrotated IAM API Key Exceeds 90 Days Age
description: Active IAM API keys have been detected with creation dates older than 90 days without cryptographic key rotation.
rationale: Static long-lived API keys accumulate exposure risks across multiple developers, logs, workstation caches, and continuous integration runners.

remediation.summary: Rotate long-lived API keys and implement automated secret management (e.g., IBM Secrets Manager).
remediation.ibmcloud_cli:
ibmcloud iam api-key-create <NEW_KEY_NAME> -d 'Rotated key' --file key.json
ibmcloud iam api-key-delete <OLD_KEY_ID> --force
remediation.console_steps:
1. In IBM Cloud Console, open Manage > Access (IAM) > API keys.
2. Generate a new API key and update applications.
3. Delete the stale API key.

title: IAM Allowed IP Address Restrictions Not Configured
description: The account does not enforce source IP address allowlisting for IAM user sessions and API calls.
rationale: Without network origin controls, stolen cloud administrator credentials can be utilized from anywhere globally, including anonymized VPNs and Tor exit nodes.

remediation.summary: Configure allowed IP address ranges for user login and administrative operations.
remediation.console_steps:
1. Go to Manage > Access (IAM) > Settings.
2. In 'IP address restrictions', specify your enterprise egress CIDR ranges.
